content.text: All 12 green. Let me confirm the type-checker is also clean, since the point-free `.map(itemBasePremium)` change touches an inference site.

Clean. Refactor phase complete.

## Refactor summary

All 12 tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Three refactorings applied, one at a time with a test run after each.

**1. Naming (evaluated first)** — `alikeGroupBasePremium` → `itemGroupBasePremium`, and the `alikeItems` parameters in it and `formsABlock` → `items`. The "alike" qualifier restated a guarantee the caller already provides: `groupByType` is the only caller and by construction yields same-type groups. Naming a parameter after a precondition the function doesn't itself check reads like a claim about the argument rather than a description of it. `policyBasePremium` was reviewed and kept — it accurately describes summing group premiums across the policy.

**2. Duplication (Rule 3)** — `sumOfItemBasePremiums` had its own `reduce` that re-implemented the summation `sumOf` already provides. Now `sumOf(items.map(itemBasePremium))`, so summing exists in exactly one place. The point-free `itemBasePremium` is safe under `.map` because it takes a single parameter, so the extra index/array arguments are ignored.

**3. Simplification (Rule 4)** — `groupByType` was a mutable-`Map` accumulation loop with a `??` fallback. Rewritten as distinct-types-then-select:

```ts
const types = new Set(items.map((item) => item.type));
return [...types].map((type) => items.filter((item) => item.type === type));
```

This removes the mutation and the conditional. Ordering is preserved: `Set` iterates in insertion order, so groups still appear in first-appearance order — which the "3 runes + 3 moonstones" test depends on only for grouping, not ordering, but is worth keeping stable.

**APP mass**, block-pricing cluster (`sumOf`, `formsABlock`, `sumOfItemBasePremiums`, `groupByType`, `itemGroupBasePremium`, `policyBasePremium`): **75 → 56 (Δ −19)**. The bulk is `groupByType` at 22 → 15 (dropped one conditional and the mutating `set`/`get` invocations) and `sumOfItemBasePremiums` at 14 → 10 (dropped its own loop and `+` invocation, gaining one `map` loop but reusing `sumOf`).

Note the mass reduction here did not cost clarity — the declarative `groupByType` is the version I'd defend on Rule 2 grounds even if it scored higher.

**Known gap, left in place as instructed**: block pricing at `itemGroupBasePremium` still applies to every item type, so 3 swords would price at 60 G rather than 300 G. No active or pending test covers it, so no component-vs-main-item distinction was introduced. Worth flagging that the upcoming `it.todo("a policy covering a sword and 3 runes → insurance sum 1750 G")` and the multi-item modifier tests are the likely place this surfaces.
